items.summary: Could AI really threaten humanity by the end of this decade, or are tech companies using the fear of AI to push for more control over the technology? In this week's South Central, hosts Dhanya Rajendran and Pooja Prasanna explore whether AI could pose an existential threat to humanity, and what regulation and the debate over whether AI development needs to slow down. They are joined by Sarayu Natarajan, founder of Aapti Institute and Visiting Associate Professor at Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, and Deepthi Bathini, AI Policy and Strategy Fellow at Successif and Associate Lecturer at Anglia Ruskin University, to discuss growing concerns around artificial intelligence, the risks posed by increasingly capable AI systems, calls for a slowdown in AI development, and the challenges of regulating the technology globally. Sarayu urges caution against treating every dramatic claim about AI as settled fact. She argues that while AI’s capabilities are rapidly advancing, the conversation is also shaped by marketing, billion-dollar valuations and geopolitical competition, making it important to separate the technology itself from the hype surrounding it. She adds that AI could also be used by bad actors to create weapons, spread misinformation and “sow disharmony” in countries, saying that there are “multiple pathways” through which AI could potentially pose a threat to humanity. The discussion also examines the controversial “Hugging Face incident”, where AI agents appeared to communicate and carry out an unauthorized hack without direct human prompting. Sarayu says the real question is not whether the agents had agency, but whether humans designed incentives that led them to behave that way. She says systemic risks include algorithmic bias and problematic government use of AI, while catastrophic risks involve large-scale harm through cyberattacks or bioweapons, and existential risks concern scenarios where humanity itself could cease to exist. करने का समय दे दिया. हालांकि, कोर्ट ने साफ कहा कि अडाणी एंटरप्राइजेज को यह आखिरी मौका है और इसके बाद आगे कोई स्थगन नहीं मिलेगा. अब मामले की अगली सुनवाई 23 सितंबर को होगी. मालूम हो कि रवि एक स्वतंत्र पत्रकार हैं. उन्होंने अडाणी-हिंडनबर्ग विवाद, कॉर्पोरेट एकाधिकार और कथित गलत कामों पर लगातार रिपोर्टिंग की है. लाइव लॉ की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, जस्टिस एम के ठक्कर की अदालत में अडाणी की ओर से पेश वकील ने कुछ कानूनी और तथ्यात्मक पहलू रिकॉर्ड पर लाने के लिए समय मांगा. नायर के वकील अभिक चिमनी ने इसका विरोध किया और अंतरिम राहत की मांग की. उन्होंने कहा कि मामला अपील स्तर पर है और एक निजी शिकायतकर्ता को बार-बार स्थगन नहीं मिलना चाहिए. साथ ही उन्होंने दलील दी कि उनके मुवक्किल (नायर) को एक दिन भी जेल में नहीं बिताना चाहिए. इस बीच अदालत ने नोटिस जारी होने के बाद शिकायतकर्ता को अपना पक्ष रखने का मौका देना उचित माना, लेकिन साथ ही कहा कि वह मामले में आगे कोई स्थगन नहीं होगा. मालूम हो कि रवि नायर को 17 सितंबर को गांधीनगर सत्र न्यायालय ने गैर-जमानती वारंट रद्द करने की अर्जी खारिज करने के बाद न्यायिक हिरासत में भेज दिया था. इससे पहले 3 सितंबर को अदालत ने उनके जानबूझकर पेश न होने की बात कही थी. केरल के रहने वाले नायर की दलील है कि सुनवाई में पेशी के लिए लंबा सफर और खर्च उठाना पड़ता है. बताते चलें कि ये मामला मामला अडाणी एंटरप्राइजेज की 2021 की शिकायत से जुड़ा है. कंपनी का आरोप था कि नायर ने एक्स पर पोस्ट और अडाणी वॉच वेबसाइट पर लेखों के जरिए झूठे और मानहानिकारक बयान फैलाए, जिससे समूह की प्रतिष्ठा को नुकसान पहुंचा. जिसके बाद बीते 10 फरवरी 2026 को ज्यूडिशियल मैजिस्ट्रेट (फर्स्ट क्लास) ने उन्हें मानहानि का दोषी ठहराते हुए एक साल की साधारण कैद और 5,000 रुपये जुर्माना की सजा सुनाई थी. हालांकि, सत्र न्यायालय ने 9 मार्च को उनकी सजा निलंबित कर जमानत दे दी थी, बशर्ते वे अदालत में नियमित पेश होते रहें. अब वही शर्त पूरी न होने का मुद्दा हाईकोर्ट तक पहुंच गया है. नायर ने अपनी याचिका में सितंबर के दोनों आदेश रद्द करने और मार्च वाली जमानत बहाल करने की मांग है. अदालत ने राज्य सरकार और अडाणी दोनों को नोटिस जारी किया है. अडाणी पर ऐसा क्या ट्वीट किया कि पत्रकार रवि नायर को हो गई जेल नियम बदला, अडाणी छाए: 20 हजार करोड़ की एफसीआई की साइलो योजना में अडाणी समूह का वर्चस्व?

items.title: Arbitration may rhyme with "arbitrary" but arbitral proceedings can't be arbitrary: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently quipped that though the word "arbitration" rhymes with "arbitrary", arbitral proceedings cannot be conducted in an arbitrary or biased manner [ Arth Micro Finance Private Ltd & Ors. v. Shivalik Small Finance Bank Ltd. ]. In an order passed on September 17, a Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran emphasised that bias and lack of consent render the initiation of arbitration invalid in law. "Arbitration, though rhymes with it, cannot result in an arbitrary measure, even in the appointment of an Arbitral Tribunal," the Court said. Hence, it set aside a High Court order that had dismissed an appeal against three interim directions passed by an arbitral tribunal under Section 17 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran The Court was hearing an appeal filed by Arth Micro Finance challenging interim orders passed by an arbitral tribunal appointed at the instance of Shivalik Small Finance Bank. The tribunal had issued directions freezing several bank accounts of Arth, permitting Shivalik to take over movable and immovable properties and ordering the transfer of deposited funds into Shivalik's bank accounts. Aggrieved by these directions, Arth approached the High Court under Section 37 of the Act. However, the High Court dismissed the appeal on grounds of limitation as no application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act had been filed. Supreme Court Arbitration, though rhymes with it, cannot result in an arbitrary measure, even in the appointment of an Arbitral Tribunal Before the top court, Arth contended that the tribunal was appointed unilaterally despite explicit objections raising allegations of bias and close links between the arbitrator and Shivalik. Finding no evidence of consent from Arth for the appointment, the Supreme Court held the entire initiation of arbitration to be non est in law. "We have to remind ourselves that this was done in the wake of the clear objection to the appointment of the Arbitral Tribunal and the allegation of bias raised against the said Arbitral Tribunal. The orders passed at the first instance, are also arbitrary in nature," the Court said. Consequently, the top court quashed all three interim orders and directed Shivalik to remit any transferred funds within one week, warning that failure to comply would attract compound interest at 18% per annum. items.title: How Humayun landed a PSC candidate before Supreme Court over one mark
items.summary: The Supreme Court was recently called to decide a dispute over the answer to a question that had Mughal emperor Humayun and the Humayunnama as one of the answer options in a State recruitment exam [ UPSSSC v. Ashok Yadav ]. The dispute arose from a 2016 examination conducted by the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Service Selection Commission (UPSSSC) for recruitment to 3,133 posts of Village Development Officer. One of the general knowledge questions asked candidates to identify the incorrectly matched pair from the following options: Baburnama–Babur, Shahjahannama–Mohammad Tahir, Humayunnama–Humayun and Tuzuk-e-Jahangiri–Jahangir. The Commission treated “Shahjahannama–Mohammad Tahir” as the correct answer to the question. The UPSSC's basis for choosing the right pair was subject-wise pairing: matching each book with the person it is about. A candidate, however, selected “Humayunnama–Humayun” as the answer, since Humayunnama was authored by Gulbadan Begum and not Humayun. The remaining options matched the books to their authors. The candidate proceeded to challenge the Commission's interpretation that this answer was wrong, arguing that he was entitled to an extra mark for choosing "Humayunnama–Humayun." This disagreement over one mark eventually reached a Bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi of the Supreme Court. Justices Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi The Court held that the candidate could not claim the mark since the question did not specify that authorship was the basis on which the pairs had to be examined. The Court opined that the Commission's approach was a plausible one, and refused to grant the candidate relief. The Court acknowledged the unusual consequence of its conclusion: the candidate appeared to have lost the mark precisely because he knew who had actually written Humayunnama . However, that itself is not a ground for the Court to interfere in such matters in the exercise of its judicial review powers, the Bench held. “ It is possible that if he had not known that Humayun is not the author of Humayunnama, he may not have opted for option ’C’. Therefore, one may feel that the writ petitioner is being punished for having knowledge about a historical fact. But that is not the ground to test the correctness of the question or the answer while exercising the power of judicial review, ” the Court said. items.title: Supreme Court rejects Centre's review petition against verdict on private complaints in Companies Act fraud cases
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a review petition filed by the Central government against its judgment holding that a special court cannot take cognisance of certain Companies Act offences linked to fraud based on private complaints. [Union of India v. State of Telangana] A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices K Vinod Chandran and Joymalya Bagchi was dealing with the Centre's plea seeking review of the Court's January 9 judgment concerning the bar contained in the second proviso to Section 212(6) of the Companies Act, 2013. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice Vinod Chandran While declining to reconsider the judgment, the Court clarified that the Central government was at liberty to exercise its powers under the second proviso to Section 212(6) and authorise any officer, by a general or special order in writing, to institute the complaint. The clarification assumes significance since Section 212(6) permits cognisance upon a written complaint by the Director of the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) or an officer of the Central government authorised by a general or special written order. Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati , appearing for the Centre, raised concerns over the implications of the judgment for investigations which were not conducted by the SFIO, including those involving the Registrar of Companies (ROC). The Court indicated that the Centre could address such situations by exercising its statutory power to authorise an officer to institute the complaint. It made clear that its earlier ruling concerning the maintainability of a private complaint did not prevent the government from using the route expressly provided under Section 212(6). The judgment under review had been delivered by a Bench of Justices JK Maheshwari and K Vinod Chandran in January this year. The case arose from a dispute concerning the management and control of a private company. A private complaint alleged, among other things, that former directors had illegally convened a meeting, fabricated resolutions and made false statutory filings with the ROC. The Special Court for Economic Offences at Hyderabad had taken cognisance of offences under Sections 448 and 451 of the Companies Act along with several offences under the Indian Penal Code (IPC). items.title: DHJS officer Reetesh Singh appointed new Registrar General of Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has appointed Delhi Higher Judicial Service (DHJS) officer Reetesh Singh as its new registrar general. At present, Singh is posted as Principal Secretary (Law, Justice and Legislative Affairs), Government of NCT of Delhi. "Hon'ble the Chief Justice has been pleased to appoint Mr. Reetesh Singh, an Officer of Delhi Higher Judicial Service, presently posted as Principal Secretary (Law, Justice and Legislative Affairs), Govt. of NCT of Delhi, as Registrar General in this Court on deputation basis, with effect from 22.09.2026," read a notification issued by the High Court. Singh has been given the assignment after the elevation of the High Court's former registrar general Arun Bhardwaj as an additional judge of the High Court. Bhardwaj took oath of office on September 21. [Read Notification]

items.title: NLSIU's LawSoc cancels Umar Khalid documentary screening
items.summary: The Law and Society Committee (LawSoc) at National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru has decided not to proceed with the screening of Lalit Vachani's documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid , Prisoner No. 626710 is Present . In an email to students, LawSoc said that the planned screening had been met with serious threats of criminal action, intimidation, doxxing and other forms of harassment. "As LawSoc, we continue to be undeterred and committed deeply to questions of freedom and justice. Equally, we are committed to the safety and security of our own peers and the wider NLS community. Thus, after several rounds of discussions with the SBA and administration, we have decided not to proceed with the screening of the film, but to instead engage informatively and critically on the questions relating to criminal justice that the present moment raises," the email added. The email further stated that the decision was not a cancellation of Political Prisoners Day, nor was it a decision to step away from the conversation. The screening was originally scheduled for September 14, to mark Political Prisoners' Day (September 13) and 6 years since Khalid's arrest in a case linked to the 2020 Delhi riots. The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) had been campaigning for the screening's cancellation since it was first announced. It was then deferred to September 19 , citing logistical and security considerations around the Ganesh Chaturthi festival. At the time, LawSoc said that the move was not a response to pressure. According to sources, LawSoc and the NLSIU administration discussed the matter at length. Their assessment was that the screening was "not exactly in the white" on legality, and that a Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) social media post may have signalled scrutiny to come. Public Screening of a Documentary film that has not yet been Certified by the CBFC is a violation of the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been sought under the Act. items.title: TERES joins Singapore Courts’ approved list for real-time transcription services
items.summary: Legal technology company TERES has been included in the Singapore Courts’ list of approved providers of real-time transcription services. The approval allows TERES to provide such services for hearings before the Supreme Court, including the Court of Appeal, the High Court and the Singapore International Commercial Court, as well as the State Courts and the Family Justice Courts. Speaking to Bar & Bench , TERES Chief Executive Officer Vikas Mahendra said the company was included on the list after a formal due diligence process carried out by the Singapore Courts. “ Representatives of the court had the opportunity to view our offering during the TechLaw.Fest in Singapore in 2024. We then wrote to the courts officially as directed on the Courts' website expressing our interest to be included in the list maintained by the courts. This was followed by a formal process of due diligence carried out by the courts after which we were included ,” Mahendra said. He added that inclusion in the list was necessary for TERES to provide real-time transcription services before the Singapore Courts. “ Only vendors included in the list of providers approved by the Singapore Courts and published on their website can provide real-time transcription services before the courts. Therefore, this approval was a necessary step ,” Mahendra said. Vikas Mahendra The Singapore Judiciary has clarified that it does not make any representation regarding the services provided by vendors on the list. Court users wishing to avail themselves of such services engage the vendors directly. TERES uses a combination of artificial intelligence and human review for transcription. Its speech-to-text system prepares a first draft as the hearing proceeds, which is manually reviewed in real time by trained correctors. The transcript is then reviewed again before being certified and issued to the parties. According to the company, final transcripts are typically delivered within two to three hours after the hearing ends. TERES also offers hyperlinking of document references in transcripts to the hearing bundle, besides electronic hearing bundles, electronic presentation of evidence and AI-driven live interpretation reviewed by expert translators. items.title: Can't force people at workplace to wear Santa caps: Allahabad High Court
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently observed that people cannot be forced to wear Santa Claus caps in violation of their right to faith and belief [Vikram Singh @ Vishwa Vikram Singh v State of UP and Another] Justice Saurabh Srivastava made the observation while dealing with a case in which 'V Bazar' employees had allegedly been forced to wear Santa Claus red caps by their superiors in 2022. "The documents which have been appended along with affidavit in support of the application, crystal clearly shows that compulsion has been created by the superior authorities of "V Bazar" for wearing Santa Claus Red Cap which is somehow hurting the sentiments of the different faith and beliefs and this type of action is not permitted in the democratic system of the country wherein every citizen is free to follow his/her faith and belief," the Court said. The Court added that it may disturb the peaceful and harmonious atmosphere of a working place. "Applicant along with his superior authorities are hereby warned not to repeat this type of instructions in shape of disturbing the peaceful and harmonious atmosphere of the working place amongst their employee." Justice Saurabh Srivastava One of the accused in the case had approached the Court seeking to quash the proceedings and summons issued to him by Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) Agra in the case under Section 298 (uttering, words, etc., with deliberate intent to wound the religious feelings of any person) and 504 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). It was argued before the High Court that since the offences are non-cognizable in nature, the CJM could not have treated it as a police case. Agreeing with the submission, the Court noted that Section 2(d) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) provides that a chargesheet submitted by the Investigating Officer in a case of non-cognizable offence has to be deemed as a complaint. "In view of the above explanation, charge sheet submitted by the concerned Investigating Officer in the present case under Sections 298, 504 I.P.C. shall be treated as complaint and it is to be decided as complaint and the learned Magistrate fell in legal error by taking cognizance as State case and the orders passed by him is, therefore, liable to be set aside," the Court ruled. Accordingly, the Court quashed the order summoning the accused. However, it also clarified that the trial court can treat the case as a complaint case, if required

items.title: Karnataka High Court upholds tax refund of ₹27.13 crore to Myntra and Cult.fit co-founder Mukesh Bansal
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has set aside the revision proceedings initiated by the Income Tax (IT) Department against entrepreneur Mukesh Bansal in relation to a refund of over ₹27.13 crore return for the Assessment Year 2019-2020 [Mukesh Bansal v Principal Commissioner of Income Tax, Bengaluru-2] Justice S Sunil Dutt Yadav held the notice issued to Bansal, who co-founded Myntra, Cult.Fit, and Meraki Labs, for hearing of the revision proceedings was without any jurisdiction and required to be set aside. The Court ruled that the intimation under Section 143(1) could not be treated as an order for the purpose of revision of power under Section 263 of the IT Act. "The treating of an intimation under Section 143(1) as a notice of demand is by a fiction of law which cannot be extended to deeming the passing of an Assessment Order prior to an intimation," the Court said on September 18. Justice Sunil Dutt Yadav Bansal had declared income of ₹231.73 crore for the year 2019-20, tax liability of ₹82.55 crore and claimed a refund of ₹6.07 Lakh. The same was processed. The dispute began when Bansal sought a condonation of delay in January 2024 and filed a revised return for AY 2019-20. In the revised return, Bansal claimed the Repurchase of Employee Stock Options (ESOPs) under the head of 'Salary' rather than 'Capital Gains' as previously filed. Due to this, Bansal claimed he was eligible for a refund of ₹27.13 crore. While the revised return was processed and the refund was ordered, the same was sought to be revised by the Revenue. Bansal moved the Court, arguing that power under Section 263 could be exercisable only against an order passed in the proceedings under the IT Act, while an intimation under Section 143(1) is not an order. Considering the Revenue’s powers in this regard, the Court found that the adjustments permitted under Section 143(1) are narrow and limited, with not much discretion. In contrast, the Court said that Section 143(2) provides for scrutiny and leads to the passing of an Assessment Order. “Having lost out on time to initiate proceedings under Section 143(2), the Revenue cannot readily resort to the proceedings under Section 263 by construing without establishing that the intimation under Section 143(1) of the I.T. items.title: Some North Indian States not declaring cancer as notifiable disease: Supreme Court informed
items.summary: Some North Indian States with high tobacco and alcohol consumption are unwilling to declare cancer as a notifiable disease, the Supreme Court was told on Monday [Anurag Srivastava v. Union of India and Ors.] . A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a plea seeking uniform reporting of cancer cases across the country. Advocate Gaurav Bansal, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that nationwide data on cancer cases was necessary for the National Cancer Registry to plan treatment and identify areas requiring greater screening. “The North Indian States who have tobacco and alcohol, they are not willing to notify it. As far as the uniform plan is concerned, because the data is needed by the National Cancer Registry, and then they will plan how to treat and where to do more screening and all those things,” submitted Bansal. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana The plea was filed by former AIIMS doctor Dr Anurag Srivastava seeking directions to the Centre and States to declare cancer a notifiable disease and establish a centralised, real-time digital cancer registry. The plea has sought mandatory reporting of cancer cases so that more comprehensive data can be used for early detection, treatment planning and allocation of healthcare resources. The issue came up before the Court after a Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare recommended that cancer be declared a notifiable disease across all States and Union Territories . The Committee had held that systematic reporting would generate real-time data, strengthen surveillance and help in developing region-specific strategies and allocating resources. In August , the Supreme Court had asked the 19 States and Union Territories that had not yet notified cancer to consider doing so. The Court had noted that 17 of the 36 States and Union Territories had already notified cancer as a notifiable disease and called for a uniform policy on mandatory reporting. The Court directed the remaining States and Union Territories to consider the Parliamentary Committee's recommendations and file compliance affidavits. items.title: Khaitan's Swathy Ramanath joins Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas as Partner
items.summary: Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co has announced the appointment of Swathy Ramanath as a Partner in the Firm’s Infrastructure, Energy and Project Finance practice, in Bengaluru. Ramanath is a 2011 alumna of National Law School of India University. She has 15 years of experience advising on complex matters across the Projects, Infrastructure and Energy sectors. She has extensive experience in project contracts, concessions and bid processes, mergers & acquisitions and financing, and has advised on a wide range of transactions and assignments involving critical infrastructure assets. Her practice spans power transmission, airports, conventional and renewable power, railways and allied infrastructure, as well as other critical infrastructure sectors. She has also advised clients on disputes relating to her areas of sectoral focus. Her experience also includes advising on the establishment and growth of Global Capability Centres (GCCs), giving her a broader understanding of the infrastructure, regulatory, commercial and transactional considerations relevant to businesses operating and expanding in India. Prior to joining SAM, Ramanath was a Partner at Khaitan & Co, which she had joined in 2011 as an Associate and has now exited as a Partner. Commeting on the appointment, Managing Partners Pallavi Shroff and Akshay Chudasama said, “Swathy’s extensive experience across infrastructure, energy and projects, including her work across critical infrastructure sectors such as power, airports and railways, complements and strengthens SAM’s existing capabilities in these areas. items.title: Fair complexion, height, physique, English proficiency can't prove person follows Christianity: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently held that the fair complexion of a person, tall height, good physique, and proficiency in Tamil and English are not reasons to claim that the person practices Christianity [ M Ravikumar v District Level Vigilance Committee & Ors. ]. Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy made the observation while setting aside a District Level Vigilance Committee order which had rejected the community certificate of one M Ravikumar, a Customs Department officer. Ravikumar had claimed to belong to the Hindu Adi Dravidar community after being reconverted to Hinduism, following his birth into a Christian family. The Committee had relied, among other things, on Ravikumar and his family's physical and linguistic characteristics, noting that they were fair-skinned, tall, well-built, spoke Tamil and English and had curly hair. The High Court, however, rejected the relevance of these factors while examining the religion of a person, observing, "While, whether the petitioner follows the Hindu gods or Christianity, will be relevant, the reasoning that the petitioner and his family members are very fair in colour, they are tall and having good physique and speak Tamil and English and have curly hair, may not have any relevance. It had also cited his father's burial in a Christian cemetery and concluded that Ravikumar had not been accepted back into the Adi Dravidar community after his reconversion. items.title: Supreme Court refuses to cancel bail of murder accused who said "money and power can get you anything"
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a plea seeking the cancellation of bail granted to a murder accused who, after release on bail, had claimed on a social media video that "money and power can get you anything in this country." A Bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath , Augustine George Masih , and Sandeep Mehta dismissed the appeal filed by the complainant challenging the bail order passed by the Punjab and Haryana High Court. During the hearing, the apex court remarked that the accused, one Vishal, was merely celebrating his regained personal liberty and dismissed the suggestion that his post demonstrated illicit influence of wealth or clout. "Alright. It’s an achievement. He gained his liberty, he was celebrating. If he had money and power, he would have never gotten inside. The money was the lawyer’s fee," the Court orally observed. The matter arose from an incident that took place in October 2022 over a land dispute regarding the installation of a tin shed in Haryana's Berla village. According to the prosecution, the accused struck a woman with a stick ( danda ) and allegedly dealt an axe blow to the head of one Gajanand, who later succumbed to his injuries. Vishal was arrested on October 28, 2022. The Additional Sessions Judge rejected his bail plea in February 2024, following which his successive bail applications before the High Court were also turned down four times. However, on April 23, 2026, the Punjab and Haryana High Court granted Vishal regular bail in his fifth petition. Justice Rajesh Bhardwaj of the High Court noted that the allegations did not match the postmortem report, as no incised wounds were found on the deceased and the weapon recovered was a stick rather than an axe. The High Court also held that all material eyewitnesses had already been examined and that Vishal had spent over three years and five months in pre-trial detention with only 8 out of 31 witnesses examined, thereby violating his constitutional right to a speedy trial under Article 21. Aggrieved by the grant of bail and relying upon the boastful video published by the accused on social media upon his release, the complainant, Rajbala, approached the apex court seeking cancellation of the relief. items.title: Delhi High Court notifies new rules for Senior Advocate designation; conduct, ethics, pro bono work made factors
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has notified new rules for the designation of lawyers as Senior Advocates, replacing the framework issued in March 2024. As per the new rules, an advocate's fairness, courtroom conduct, professional ethics, role as a mentor to junior advocates, pro bono work and standing in the legal fraternity will be taken into account while considering conferment of gown. Pertinently, the new rules have done away with the committee for designating Senior Advocates which was provided under the earlier rules. Under the new rules, a permanent secretariat headed by an officer of the rank of registrar will oversee the designation process and the designation will be decided directly by the full court. The secretariat will initiate the process at least once every year by inviting applications, with the notice to be published on the High Court's website and communicated to the Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA). Applicants will be given at least 21 days to apply. An advocate must ordinarily have at least 10 years of practice, should be enrolled with a Bar Council and should have mainly practised before the High Court, trial and district courts or specialised tribunals. The advocate must also be at least 40 years old, unless the full court relaxes the age requirement. The minimum practice requirement will not apply to former Delhi Higher Judicial Service (DHJS) officers who have less than 10 years of cumulative experience as judicial officers and/or at the Bar. “Canvassing by a nominee for designation as a Senior Advocate shall disqualify him for being so designated,” the rules state. The designation process can be initiated either suo motu by the full court or through an application made by an eligible advocate. After applications are received, the permanent secretariat will publish the names of applicants on the High Court website and invite suggestions and views from stakeholders within four weeks. For advocates practising before specialised tribunals and trial or district courts, views may also be sought from tribunal chairpersons and Principal District and Sessions Judges. “After the collection of information by the Permanent Secretariat, all the applications of the candidates found to be eligible along with relevant documents will be submitted to the Full Court with the approval of Hon’ble the Chief Justice,” the rules say. items.title: Delhi High Court's working strength rises to 50 after 7 new judges take oath
items.summary: With the swearing-in of seven news judges on Monday, the Delhi High Court has received a significant boost to its working strength. The addition of the seven judges has taken the High Court's working strength to 50 against its sanctioned strength of 60 judges. This could be the first time the High Court is functioning with 50 sitting judges after its sanctioned strength was raised to 60 in 2014. In 2022, the working strength of the High Court had risen to 47 . With 83% of its sanctioned strength now functioning, the High Court, which has witnessed a continuous increase in the number of commercial matters, will have more judges to handle cases and improve its disposal rate. Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya today administered oath of office to Justices Nivedita Anil Sharma , Nisha Sahay Saxena , Sanjay Sharma , Bharat Parashar , Aditi Choudhary , Dinesh Bhatt and Arun Bhardwaj . The High Court now has 13 women judges. It will maintain the current strength of judges till next month, unless more judges are appointed. Four judges are slated to retire this year. While Justice CS Sudha is set to retire on October 8, Justice Anil Kshetarpal will retire on November 18. Justices Manoj Jain and Girish Kathpalia will demit office during the last week of 2026. Delhi High Court has an approved strength of 45 permanent judges and 15 additional judges. items.title: Suspended directors have to give confidentiality undertaking for access to resolution plan: NCLAT
items.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) has held that a resolution professional can ask suspended directors to furnish a confidentiality undertaking before providing them access to a resolution plan and other confidential material in a corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) [Mandava Prabhakar Rao Vs Navneet Gupta]. Technical Member Naresh Salecha , who was called upon to resolve an earlier split verdict by the NCLAT, agreed with the view that such a requirement does not violate the rights of suspended directors to participate CIRP. “ The resolution professional can take an undertaking from members of the erstwhile board of directors to maintain confidentiality, ” Salecha held. He said that the right of suspended directors to access resolution plans has to operate alongside their obligation to maintain confidentiality. The ruling arose from appeals filed by Mandava Prabhakar Rao, a suspended director of NSL Nagapatnam Power and Infratech Limited. The dispute concerned the company's 20th Committee of Creditors (CoC) meeting held on July 16, 2024. Rao had nominated Nelluri Bapuji to represent the suspended management in CoC meetings. Bapuji had participated in several earlier meetings. However, at the 20th meeting, he was asked to leave after failing to furnish a written authorisation and a confidentiality undertaking. The meeting involved consideration of resolution plans submitted for the company. Rao challenged Bapuji's exclusion, arguing that it deprived the suspended management of its statutory right to participate in the CIRP and access material necessary to make representations before the CoC. The resolution professional maintained that the 20th CoC meeting involved commercially sensitive material and that access could be granted only after compliance with confidentiality requirements. The appeals were initially heard by a two-member NCLAT Bench comprising Judicial Member Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma and Technical Member Jatindranath Swain. The Bench delivered a split verdict on November 10, 2025. Justice Sharma upheld the insolvency process while Swain took the view that the exclusion of the suspended director’s representative from the 20th CoC meeting was impermissible and warranted reopening the process from that stage. In view of the difference of opinion, the points on which the two members disagreed were referred to Technical Member Naresh Salecha for determination as the third member. Salecha agreed with Justice Sharma's view

items.title: Movie is not IT software even if delivered via digital link or hard disk: Bombay High Court
items.summary: A cinematographic film is not information technology software under Goods and Services Tax (GST) law even if it is delivered via digital link or hard disk, the Bombay High Court recently held [Dharma Productions Pvt Ltd v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.]. Hence, it set aside a tax demand of over ₹79.7 crore levied on Dharma Productions Pvt. Ltd. and Dharmatic Entertainment Pvt. Ltd. The judgment was passed by a division bench of Justice MS Karnik and Justice Sandesh D Patil on September 10. Justice MS Karnik, Justice Sandesh Patil The State Tax Department had raised tax demands for the period between FY 2017-18 and FY 2020-21. Tax authorities argued that delivering film content through digital links or hard disks brought the transaction under IT software services (SAC 998340). This attracted an 18 percent GST rate. Dharma Productions countered that licensing film rights falls under Heading 9973 (SAC 997332), which was subject to a lower rate of 12 percent GST prior to the amendment notification on October 1, 2021. The bench rejected the revenue department's position on digital delivery modes. It stressed that passive film content fails to meet the statutory definition of software under the Rate notification. “There is no finding, much less a finding, as to how a cinematographic film, a passive audio visual work, incapable of execution, manipulation or inter-activity could ever satisfy the statutory definition 'information technology software',” the order. The bench further emphasised that the mode of delivery remains irrelevant to tax classification. “Whether content is transmitted physically (encrypted hard disks) or electronically, the mode of delivery cannot determine classification, which must turn on the essential character of the supply. Equating “digital content” with “software”, the core error underlying the impugned orders, has no statutory basis,” the judgment said. The State also raised a preliminary objection regarding the availability of an alternative remedy before the appellate tribunal. The High Court held that writ jurisdiction under Article 226 was maintainable due to a foundational jurisdictional error. The bench affirmed that an authority misconstruing statutory entries to assume taxing power acts without jurisdiction. Hence, it quashed the assessment and appellate orders. items.title: [Courting Controversy] The toll that builds the road: UPI’s Highway Moment
items.summary: India’s national highway story captures how large public infrastructure comes into its own. The National Highways, expanded and maintained through toll collection, did not merely connect cities. They transformed how trade moved, how businesses reached new markets, and how a fragmented economy became a single connected one, because the toll collected ensured the roads stayed safe and well maintained. While the national highways represent an infrastructure-led way of connecting India, the last decade has seen a different kind of connective tissue emerge in India, that is, fintech. Online payments through Unified Payments Interface (" UPI "), have not only made everyday transactions cashless, faster, cheaper and more accessible, but have also been instrumental in drawing India’s vast unorganised sector into a common, formal fold. The success of UPI is owed to a simple fact: payments run on convenience, and convenience unifies the economy. Credit and debit cards illustrate the point well: they carry a charge well above 1%, and yet they are significantly utilised for their efficiency and frictionless checkout. Cash, in fact, has never been truly free; it simply hides its costs, as the neighbourhood vegetable vendor accepting only cash stays invisible to the tax net. UPI has managed to streamline real-time bank transfers just as credit cards had streamlined payments at the checkout counter, while also pulling unorganised sector’s transactions onto the books as traceable, legitimate income. Having become the backbone of India’s daily commerce, UPI is now poised for its next big leap: from a free payments platform supported by government subsidy, to a self-sustaining system built to further expand digital payments. Recently, the central government notified a Merchant Discount Rate (" MDR ") of 0.4% on UPI person-to-merchant transactions above INR 2,000, effective from 15 October 2026, a modest charge for a system that is reshaping how millions of people transact. This charge, notably, is selective. Ordinary person-to-person UPI transfers remain entirely free, no matter the amount. The charge applies only to merchant payments above INR 2,000. Thin-margin sectors such as railways, telecom, insurance, fuel, and agricultural inputs, get a flat charge of INR 5 per transaction and capital market transactions get their own bracket at 0.02% per transaction, capped at INR 300. items.title: Delhi High Court stays JNU order imposing fine on students for smiling at protesters
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently stayed Jawaharlal Nehru University's (JNU) order imposing ₹19,000 fine on certain students allegedly for merely smiling at certain protestors [Mr C Arjun & Ors v Jawaharlal Nehru University] . Justice Jasmeet Singh observed that the students' conduct "does not constitute any infraction which can be categorised as indiscipline of any sort". The Court observed that JNU's action strikes a blow at the students' fundamental rights and cannot be allowed. "I cannot lose sight of the fact that the petitioners are students in the respondent University and as a student, the right to express dissent/demonstrate and/or to express support by way of cheering for a demonstration, to my mind, constitutes a valuable right which cannot be allowed to be curbed or interdicted in any manner. The students/petitioners cannot be allowed to be punished for an act of such a nature," the Court observed. Justice Jasmeet Singh Delhi High Court The right to express dissent/demonstrate and/or to express support by way of cheering for a demonstration, to my mind, constitutes a valuable right which cannot be allowed to be curbed or interdicted in any manner. Justice Singh was hearing a petition filed by the students challenging a show cause notice dated January 15, 2026, issued by the office of the Chief Proctor, along with the office orders dated February 2, 2026 imposing fine on the students. The notice had later been upheld by subsequent appellate orders dated March 30. The show cause notice accused some students of aggressively shaking camera stands and vandalising the university's facial recognition technology (FRT) system. Three students were accused of encouraging and supporting the act by clapping and sloganeering during an incident on November 21, 2025. The petitioners denied any involvement, stating they were, at best, seen smiling at the protestors. After considering the case, the High Court found a prima facie case in the students' favour. Therefore, it stayed the University's order. Advocates Abhik Chimni, Moksha Sharma, Pranjal Abrol, Gurupal Singh, Ayan Dasgupta and Tushar Chandra represented the petitioner students. Senior Standing Counsel Ginny Jetley Rautray and advocate Arnav Tandon represented JNU. items.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to issue a Red Corner Notice through Interpol to trace an individual called Adeeshwar Singhal who is accused of making scandalous allegations against the judiciary [ Court On Its Own Motion Vs Adeeshwar Singhal ]. The Division Bench of Justice Navin Chawla and Justice Ravinder Dudeja passed the order to secure Singhal’s physical presence in court in suo motu contempt of court proceedings initiated against him. “We direct the Central Bureau of Investigation to issue a Red Corner Notice through INTERPOL against the respondent (Singhal) for securing his presence in compliance of our orders, including the non-bailable warrants (NBWs),” the Court directed. On September 18, Singhal joined the Court proceedings through video conference and engaged in disruptive conduct. "We will ensure that you come to court, don’t think we will leave you like this. You are making a mockery of the proceedings and making allegations. Either you come here or we will get you here," Justice Chawla warned. Justice Navin Chawla and Justice Ravinder Dudeja Standing Counsel Amit Tiwari informed the Court that Singhal had traveled from India to Italy in 2024 and has not returned since then. A Delhi Police inspector told the Court that the IP address from which Singhal had joined the proceedings during a previous hearing in April was found to be in California at the United States of America. items.title: Forcing parties into mediation is always a bad idea: Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani
items.summary: Forcing parties into mediation is always a bad idea and there is no universally right stage at which parties must attempt settlement, Delhi High Court judge Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani said at the Commercial Mediation Conclave 2026. Speaking at the event, organised by The PACT and Poovayya & Co, Justice Bhambhani said the appropriate stage for mediation would depend on the nature of the dispute and the parties’ genuine willingness to explore a settlement. “I think what is or is not the right time to start mediation depends on the dispute. Forcing parties to mediation is always a bad idea. There are times when parties have been in litigation for very long, they have suffered the battle fatigue and all of that, the litigation fatigue and that's when it dawns on them that maybe we have been walking the wrong road .” He added that parties may become more receptive to mediation once the strengths and weaknesses of their respective cases become clearer. In disputes involving continuing commercial relationships, such as construction contracts, parties may also have practical reasons to preserve their association. Justice Bhambhani was speaking during a fireside chat on Mediation in Construction Disputes along with former Supreme Court judge Justice Hima Kohli. The session was moderated by Mehak Oberoi , author of Construction Mediation . The event also saw the launch of Mehak Oberoi’s book, Construction Mediation: A Practical Handbook , by Justice Anup Bhambhani and Justice Kholi. It focuses on the practical use of mediation in construction and infrastructure disputes, including preparation, technical claims, negotiations and settlement. On who should act as a mediator, Justice Bhambhani described mediation as a “standalone and extremely soft and specific skill”. He said that a mediator need not necessarily be a technical expert in the subject matter but must understand the “pathology” of the dispute. He added that technical assistance could be taken where required in specialised disputes such as patents or construction matters Justice Bhambhani agreed that government officers were often “petrified at taking a call” and suggested that high-powered committees of senior officers could support and approve settlements, reducing the fear attached to individual decision-making. items.title: Gujarat government is not serious about expeditious disposal of arbitration cases: Former Justice Harsha Devani
items.summary: Born in Amreli district of Gujarat, Justice Harsha Devani’s path to the judiciary was anything but conventional. After completing her schooling across Assam, Bihar and Gujarat, she earned her MSc in Microbiology before pursuing an LL.B. at Sir LA Shah Law College, Ahmedabad. She enrolled as an advocate with the Bar Council of Gujarat in 1992. She served as an assistant government pleader and additional public prosecutor, mastering constitutional, civil, and criminal law. Justice Devani was elevated to the Gujarat High Court bench on October 8, 2004 and confirmed as a permanent judge in 2007. She served with distinction until her retirement in March 2020. She continues to be a sought-after judge even long after retirement. Today, her deep expertise and humanity make her a revered voice in commercial dispute resolution. In this candid chat with Bar & Bench's Neha Joshi, Justice Devani offers sharp, pragmatic insights into India's evolving legal landscape. She critiques the operational realities of the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre, unpacks systemic flaws in senior advocate designations and evaluates Gujarat’s potential to emerge as a premier commercial arbitration hub. My father was advising my younger brother - who is 8 years younger than me and had just graduated as an engineer - to study law because he believed that knowledge of law was essential regardless of whether one practised or not. I happened to be standing there and asked my brother to get an admission form for me as well. That was the starting point of my legal career. items.title: Israeli pharma giant Teva Israel wins tax battle before Delhi High Court against IT Department
items.summary: In a major victory for Israeli pharmaceutical company Teva Israel, the Delhi High Court has held that a ₹1,851 crore payment made by Ranbaxy Laboratories to Teva Israel under a settlement agreement is not taxable in India [Teva Pharma Vs Union of India]. By way of an order passed on September 15, a bench of Justices Dinesh Mehta and Vinod Kumar said the payment could not be taxed merely because it was made by an Indian company to a foreign entity. “ Mere payment by an Indian resident to a non-resident ipso facto does not constitute an income accruing or arising in India.The transaction neither falls within any of the specific deeming provisions under Section 5(2)(b) of the Act of 1961 nor of Section 9. In the absence of both, the jurisdictional foundation for issuance of notice under section 148 collapses, ” the Court held. Ranbaxy had already deducted tax before making payment to Teva. The refund of the amount to Teva would be subject to Teva USA and Teva Israel furnishing the guarantees directed by the Court. Justice Dinesh Mehta and Justice Vinod Kumar The case concerned Atorvastatin, a cholesterol-lowering medicine sold by Pfizer under the brand name Lipitor. Ranbaxy was the first company to apply for US regulatory approval to sell a generic version of the drug. It was consequently entitled to a 180-day period during which no other applicant for the generic drug could receive approval. However, there was initially uncertainty over whether Ranbaxy would receive final approval on time. In December 2010, Ranbaxy India, its US subsidiary and Teva USA entered into an agreement governing what would happen if Ranbaxy was unable to use its exclusivity. Under the agreement, Ranbaxy would selectively waive or relinquish its exclusivity in favour of Teva USA if Teva issued a valid “Ready Date Notice” after satisfying stipulated conditions concerning regulatory approval and its readiness to launch the drug. Teva USA issued such a notice on November 23, 2011. Ranbaxy disputed its validity. Teva USA then instituted proceedings before a US court seeking enforcement of the agreement. The dispute was settled with effect from November 30, 2011, the same day on which Ranbaxy received final approval for its generic drug. Ranbaxy began selling Atorvastatin in the United States the following day. Ranbaxy earned around $700 million in profits during the six-month exclusivity period. items.title: Karnataka HC stays circulars deferring revised minimum wages for outsourced, contract workers
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Friday stayed the operation of circulars that direct various authorities to withhold the implementation of revised minimum wages for outsourced and contract employees [ All India Trade Union Congress & others v. State of Karnataka & others ]. Justice H T Narendra Prasad passed the order while issuing a notice to the State on three petitions challenging circulars issued by the Karnataka State Audit and Accounts Department, the Directorate of Municipal Administration and the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department (RDPR). Justice H T Narendra Prasad The petitions have been filed by the All India Trade Union Congress, Karnataka Rajya Sarkari Khayametharara Noukarara Okkuta, the All India Central Council of Trade Unions (AICCTU) and others. The unions have challenged circulars dated July 29, August 10 and August 28, 2026, which direct government departments and local authorities to suspend or defer implementation of revised minimum wage rates notified by the Karnataka government on May 22. The petitioners contend that the May 22 notification continues to remain operative and that the pendency of challenges to the revised wage rates cannot justify withholding their implementation, particularly in the absence of any court order staying the notification. They have also questioned the authority and jurisdiction of the concerned departments to suspend the implementation of statutory minimum wages through administrative circulars. According to the petitions, the Karnataka government issued a final notification on May 22, revising minimum wage rates for 83 scheduled employments across the State. The unions contend that the revised notification came into force upon publication and had already been implemented by several government departments. The petitioners argue that the notification has been kept in abeyance based on purported verbal instructions from the Finance Department. A bench of Justice Prathiba M Singh and Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora noted that due to the inadequate recruitment of qualified staff, valuable equipment was also going unused. items.title: UAPA property attachment: Delhi High Court says appeal against special judge order maintainable before HC
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently held that an appeal against a special judge's decision upholding attachment of property under Section 25(6) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) is maintainable before the High Court [Aquil Ahmed v National Investigation Agency Throught the Chief Investigating Officer] . A Division Bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Ravinder Dudeja rejected the National Investigation Agency's (NIA) preliminary objection that a second appeal against an order of attachment was not maintainable. The NIA had said that Section 25(6) of the UAPA provides for only one appeal – to the special court. It also argued that Section 28 of UAPA separately provides for an appeal to the High Court against an eventual forfeiture order under Section 26. However, the Court said that forfeiture under Section 26 is a distinct action requiring a separate show-cause notice under Section 27. "Simple attachment of the property does not automatically lead to its forfeiture under Section 26 of the UAPA. In fact, a separate show cause notice is required to be given under Section 27 of the said Act, and upon hearing the concerned party, an order of forfeiture is to be passed under Section 26 of the Act. The two appeals would, therefore, be dealing with distinct stages of the proceedings which are final in their own stages," the Court observed. Justice Navin Chawla and Justice Ravinder Dudeja NIA had also said that Section 21 of the NIA Act, which provides for appeal against special court orders before the High Court, would have no application to a seizure or attachment order under UAPA, as it would amount to providing a second appeal against the attachment of property. It had also argued that even otherwise, an order passed under Section 25(6) of the UAPA is an interlocutory order against which no appeal is maintainable under Section 21 of the NIA Act. However, the Court said Section 25(6) orders are final since they conclusively adjudicate the question of seizure or attachment. "As far as the submission of the learned counsel for the respondent that there is a likelihood of a conflicting opinion being rendered by the High Court if an appeal under Section 21 of the NIA Act is held to be maintainable against an order passed under Section 25(6) of the UAPA, as a separate appeal is already provided to this Court under Section 28 of the said Act, the same does not impress us," it added. items.title: Trial courts must weed out frivolous criminal cases which are making our system an object of ridicule: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan
items.summary: Frivolous criminal cases are making India's justice system an object of ridicule before the liberal democratic world, Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said on Thursday. Trial courts must launch a special drive to weed them out, he added. He was speaking on the topic 'ethics in criminal litigation and the duties of the defence and the prosecution' at 4th Discourse organised by the Centre for Discourses on Criminal and Constitutional Jurisprudence at the India International Centre in New Delhi. The judge said that criminal cases were being registered just for consuming food, reciting poems, for participating in demonstrations, raising slogans, for commenting on social media, performing as a stand-up comedian and for so many other frivolous grounds including titles and contents of books and movies. "The accusations are ridiculous and often borders on an affront to one's intelligence. Nonetheless, registration of such criminal cases continues unabated; not only that, in some cases chargesheets are also filed leading to trial," he said. Justice Ujjal Bhuyan Criminal cases are being registered just for consuming food, reciting poems, for participating in demonstrations or raising slogans. Justice Bhuyan further focussed on pendency figures. According to the National Judicial Data Grid, as on September 17, a total of 4.27 crore criminal cases are pending across all courts in India. Of these, 4.07 crore or 95.31 percent are before the trial courts, 19.84 lakh or 4.64 percent before the High Courts and 22,143 before the Supreme Court. "When you have so many cases clogging the court system with the system unable to cope with it, almost bursting at the seams, super-imposition of such frivolous cases has only added to the unworkable burden on the trial courts," he said. Therefore, he suggested that a special drive should be launched by the trial courts to weed out frivolous criminal cases. "As I have said, these are only adding to the unworkability of the system with outcomes almost a foregone conclusion and making our system an object of ridicule before the liberal democratic world. items.title: J&K High Court stays FIR against woman booked for terminating pregnancy without husband’s consent
items.summary: The High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh has stayed criminal investigation into a complaint filed by a husband alleging that his wife terminated a 4–5-month pregnancy without his consent, allegedly with the assistance of her sister. Justice Rahul Bharti passed the interim order on a plea by the accused (the complainant's wife and her sister) to quash the first information report (FIR) registered against them. Justice Rahul Bharti The FIR against the two accused cited Section 126(2) (wrongful restraint/confinement), Section 88 (causing miscarriage), Section 351(2) (criminal intimidation), Section 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace), and Section 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. In an order passed on September 14, however, the Court expressed reservations about the FIR, expressing a prima facie observation that the allegations did not inspire confidence. "The tone and tenor of the contents of the FIR on the face of it do not inspire confidence about the narrative being set up by the respondent No. 3 (complainant-husband) against the petitioner No. 1 (complainant's wife/ accused)," the Court said. The Court also took note of the accused's submission that the police registered the FIR in haste, on the very same day that the husband presented his complaint. The Court added that this meant that there was no intervening time for the police's station house officer (SHO) to examine the nature of the allegations and accusations being made by the complainant. Holding that a prima facie case was made out, the High Court issued notice in the matter, thereby seeking the response of the State and the complainant. In the meantime, the Court directed that the investigation in the FIR shall remain stayed. The order, however, was made subject to objections that may be raised from the other side. The matter has been listed for further hearing on October 23, 2026. Advocate Irfan Khan appeared for the petitioners (accused women). items.title: Cannot separate development from human rights and dignity: Former CJI BR Gavai
items.summary: Human rights cannot be separated from questions of social and economic development, former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai said on Friday. Justice Gavai examined the deep connection between fundamental freedoms and sustainable development goals. “A person may formally possess political liberty, but the substantive value of that liberty is diminished when that person is deprived of food, education, healthcare, livelihood, or the basic conditions necessary for living a life with human dignity. Rights therefore cannot exist merely as abstractions,” the former judge said. He was delivering the ninth Chief Justice MC Chagla Memorial Lecture. He stressed that economic growth by itself is insufficient to measure human progress. “When we speak of development, who the development is for, development towards what end, and development at whose cost?" he asked. Justice Gavai recalled his experience presiding over the Supreme Court's Green Bench. He described judicial decision-making as "walking the tightrope for balancing between ecology and environment on one hand and sustainable development on the other hand." He highlighted how the judiciary balanced environmental protections with community livelihoods by establishing eco-sensitive zones near wildlife reserves and phasing out human-pulled rickshaws in Matheran in favour of battery-operated vehicles to safeguard worker dignity. He emphasised that economic growth must contribute to human dignity. “Environmental protection must sustain the conditions of life across generations after generations. We hold the resources in trust for the future generations. Public institutions must enable people to participate in those choices and seek remedy when their rights are violated,” the judge said. items.title: Yogesh Gowda murder case: Karnataka High Court suspends life sentence of seven convicts
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Friday (September 18) suspended the life sentences imposed on seven persons convicted by a trial court for the 2016 murder of BJP leader and Dharwad Zilla Panchayat member Yogesh Gowda, holding that they were entitled to be released on bail pending disposal of their criminal appeals. A Division Bench of Justice Mohammad Nawaz and Justice G Basavaraja passed the order on applications filed by the seven convicts (appellants) as part of their appeal challenging the trial court verdict. The Court also imposed various conditions for their release on bail. The appellants have been directed to execute a bond for ₹5 lakh each, along with two sureties for the like sum. They were also directed to deposit the entire fine amount imposed on them by the trial court, not leave India without the prior permission of the High Court and appear before the High Court or trial court whenever directed. Justice Mohammed Nawaz and Justice G Basavaraja Yogesh Gowda was hacked to death at a gym in Dharwad on June 15, 2016. A Special CBI Court in Bengaluru had, on April 17, 2026, sentenced former Congress MLA Vinay Kulkarni and 15 others to life imprisonment after finding them guilty of conspiring to murder Gowda. They were convicted under Sections 120-B (criminal conspiracy), 143 (unlawful assembly), 147, 148 (rioting with deadly armed weapon), 201 (causing the disappearance of evidence) and 302 (murder) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), The trial court directed that all sentences would run concurrently and ordered that ₹16 lakh from the fine amount be paid as compensation to Gowda's children. The present appeals before the High Court have been filed by seven such convicts (accused Nos. 2 to 7 and accused No. 18). Vinay Kulkarni has also filed an appeal in the matter. He and eight other convicts were granted bail by the High Court on July 31, after their life sentences were suspended . On Friday, seven more convicts were given such interim relief. Advocates Lakshmikanth G, Parameshwarappa C and Bhadravadi Siddeshwara appeared for the appellants (convicts). Special Public Prosecutor P Prasanna Kumar represented the CBI, while advocate Deepak Shetty appeared for an impleading applicant. items.title: 18 NCLT Benches holding half-day sittings due to member shortage: Bar Association to Supreme Court
items.summary: The NCLT Bar Association has moved the Supreme Court claiming that at least 18 benches of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) are holding only half-day sittings because of shortage of members. The Association has filed an intervention application in the Supreme Court's suo motu case concerning the appointment of judicial and technical members and inadequate infrastructure at the NCLT. According to the application, the sanctioned strength of the NCLT continues to be 63 members even though its jurisdiction substantially expanded after the enactment of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). As of June 30, 2026, the tribunal has 26 judicial members and 25 technical members, including the President, the plea stated The Association said that vacancies arising upon the retirement or completion of tenure of members often remain unfilled, leaving several benches operating at reduced capacity. “ The Tribunal is plagued by chronic vacancies, forcing numerous Benches to function with fewer Members .” The plea added that such vacancies were contributing to delays and mounting case arrears. It therefore sought appointment of successor members before incumbents demit office. The application further stated that a roster effective from August 24 showed that at least 18 NCLT benches are holding only half-day sittings because of retirement and shortage of members. The Bar Association also raised serious concerns about the physical infrastructure available to the NCLT in Delhi. It said roof leakage on the eighth floor of Block 3 at the CGO Complex had rendered courtrooms unsafe in September 2025. This left no courtroom available for benches V and VI and resulted in half-day sittings. The Association also complained of small courtrooms and the absence of adequate waiting areas and facilities for lawyers and litigants. The plea noted that despite earlier Delhi High Court orders concerning alternate premises and improved facilities, a permanent solution had not emerged. Renovation work that commenced at Block 3 in January 2025 was allegedly halted in April that year and remains stalled despite correspondence from the NCLT to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) Another concern raised was the absence of permanent support staff. The Association said that although the Supreme Court had earlier contemplated 246 supporting staff posts for the NCLT and NCLAT, not one of those posts have been permanently established. items.title: Unfortunate that people still prefer male child: Bombay High Court in female infanticide case
items.summary: The Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court recently rejected the bail application of a man accused in the murder of his one-month-old granddaughter [Gopinath Janku Pradhan v. State of Maharashtra]. The accused, Gopinath Janku Pradhan, allegedly conspired with his family members to kill the infant because she was the second female child born to his son. Justice MM Nerlikar expressed deep dismay over persistent gender bias. “It is deeply unfortunate that, even after 80 years of independence, people in our country still prefer a male child. This is a classic example of the murder of a girl child, because she was the second daughter and the family does not want a second daughter,” the judge observed. Justice MM Nerlikar Bombay High Court It is deeply unfortunate that, even after 80 years of independence, people in our country still prefer a male child. The case arose from Gadchiroli district. According to the prosecution, the newborn drowned in a tub. A heavy brick was placed on her back to prevent her from moving. Following the drowning, the family attempted to cover up the crime. They staged a scene, claiming an animal had entered through an open door at midnight and carried the child away. The family then attempted a rushed cremation. An alert local Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) worker grew suspicious and warned the family that the death was a police case. When the family refused to report it, she notified law enforcement directly. The authorities subsequently exhumed the child's body. The post-mortem report confirmed the cause of death was due to drowning. The defense counsel argued that no direct evidence linked Pradhan to the murder and sought parity with the child’s mother who was granted bail. Justice Nerlikar rejected the plea after noting that the incident took place inside Pradhan’s house. This meant’ the family had specific knowledge of the crime, the judge said. "Considering the conduct and the mode and manner of the crime, I am not inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail,” the High Court ruled. Advocate UE Quazi appeared for the Pradhan. Additional public prosecutor UR Phasate appeared for state. items.summary: The legal challenge to Maharashtra’s 2024 Maratha reservation law will be reheard for a third time by the Bombay High Court starting October 9. However following his elevation as the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court, a new bench has been formed which will now hear the matter afresh. The new bench is now headed by Justice MS Karnik ; Justices NJ Jamadar and SV Marne who were part of the earlier bench have been retained on the new bench. items.title: Can POSH Act cover women lawyers? What Supreme Court suggested
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday observed that the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act) cannot be applied in a straitjacket manner to women advocates [ Seema Joshi v. Bar Council of India ]. A Bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and AG Masih suggested a separate regulatory framework to protect female lawyers practicing in courts and tribunals across the country. The Court called for a joint consultation among various stakeholders to draft a comprehensive set of regulations for women in the legal profession, while examining the existing gender sensitisation rules. Justice bv nagarathna and Justice augustine george masih The Court made the observations while hearing a plea seeking statutory protections for women advocates. Examining the Gender Sensitisation and Sexual Harassment of Women at the Supreme Court of India (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Regulations, 2013, the Bench pointed out that the current framework is strictly limited to the top court's precincts. "In order to have a wider coverage of these regulations in so far as the High Courts and all courts under district judiciary as well as tribunals under Centre and State governments, other quasi-judicial authorities etc., it is necessary that a separate set of regulations are made as we find that POSH provisions cannot be applied in a straitjacket manner for the aggrieved women who belong to the legal profession, " the Court said. To address this gap, the apex court requested counsel to hold a joint consultation and draft a uniform set of regulations applicable across judicial, quasi-judicial and tribunal forums. Advocate Radhika Gautam, appearing for the Bar Council of India (BCI), submitted that she would seek instructions and endeavour to bring about a common regulation for women advocates. "We also request BCI counsel to ascertain from State Bar Councils as to whether any extant regulations are being implemented in this regard," the Court ordered. items.title: Re-thinking pet custody in matrimonial disputes
items.summary: Matrimonial litigation in India has traditionally revolved around familiar questions: Who gets the house after a matrimonial dispute? Who gets custody of the children? Who pays maintenance? These are questions that Indian courts have dealt with for decades. But as family structures evolve, another question is increasingly finding its way to the courts: who gets the pet? For many Indian households, a companion animal is no longer viewed merely as an item to be kept at home; they become a part of their everyday lives. When a marriage or long-term relationship breaks down, separation from the pet can, therefore, become another significant consequence of the matrimonial dispute. Indian law, however, contains no specific framework prescribing how a court should determine the custody, possession or visitation of a companion animal. This leaves courts to navigate the issue through existing civil, procedural and animal welfare laws. The issue is no longer hypothetical. Indian courts have increasingly been confronted with disputes concerning the custody of companion animals. The Delhi High Court’s proceedings concerning Henry , a Rottweiler, have brought the question of pet visitation directly into the matrimonial-litigation landscape. The Bombay High Court has also facilitated a mediated shared-care arrangement concerning a pet dog in a matrimonial dispute. Meanwhile, in a separate 2026 case involving three Toy Pomeranians, the Delhi High Court expressly observed that custody of an animal cannot simply be treated on the same footing as custody of an inanimate object. The question, therefore, is not whether Indian courts will encounter pet custody disputes. They already are. These cases point towards a question that Indian family law will increasingly have to confront: when a relationship between two people ends, what legal principles should determine the future of the animal that remains part of both their lives? items.title: Passive income ideas in India: Exploring ideas and options
items.summary: Creating extra revenue streams has become a necessity for individuals looking to secure their financial future in the current age. Building a reliable passive income in India involves a mix of smart asset allocation and using digital platforms to generate consistent returns. Understanding passive income in the digital age Digitalisation has redefined how earners interact with the market. Individuals now explore various passive income ideas to supplement their primary earnings. These methods range from high-yield refer and earn apps to traditional investment portfolios. Success relies on consistency and identifying regulated opportunities. The shift towards digital banking has simplified how one monitors these multiple revenue channels effectively. Market participants today prioritise liquidity and transparency when selecting their secondary income sources. Access to real-time data helps in better decision-making about which assets to hold or liquidate. As the digital economy matures, the distinction between active and passive efforts continues to blur, offering more flexibility to the average earner. Top passive income streams in 2026 Investors select these channels for their historical performance and structural transparency: Dividend-paying stocks and mutual funds: Investors receive a portion of corporate profits. This method provides periodic payouts while allowing for capital appreciation over time. Real estate and rental property income: Physical or commercial properties generate monthly rent. Real Estate Investment Trusts offer a similar benefit with lower entry costs. High-yield refer and earn programs: Financial product platforms serve as high-yielding options within the broader referral economy. These programs provide commissions for successful conversions within a regulated framework. Building a sustainable passive income in India requires: · Focusing on low-risk, high-return ventures · Diversification across multiple sectors to tackle market volatility · Strategic allocation of resources to create a more resilient financial profile The integration of technology makes these processes more efficient. This methodical approach reduces the impact of economic downturns on a personal portfolio. items.title: Theja Rio’s Angh set in Nagaland gets prestigious Platform Prize at Toronto Film Festival
items.summary: From a small Indian state with virtually no formal film industry and the rugged mountains of indigenous tribes comes a historic moment. Marking its debut at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF), Angh , from Nagaland, clinched the prestigious Platform Prize on September 21. The prize ensures direct eligibility for submission to the Academy Awards 2027. As per TIFF and the Academy's rules , a non-English language film that wins the Platform Prize can be submitted for consideration for Best International Feature Film. Helming Angh is London-based 31-year-old Nagaland native Theja Rio, making a remarkably striking feature directorial debut. Angh explores the identity crisis of a Konyak tribal leader in Nagaland. The film triumphed over works by eleven world-renowned directors for the Platform Prize. The section featured 12 handpicked entries selected from over 4000 submissions across nearly 90 countries. Set in the 1960s in a Naga village bordering former Burma, the film unfolds as an American missionary arrives in the community. As most villagers convert to Christianity and leave for greener pastures, the village leader, Angba, holds fast to his ancestral customs and traditions. His only companions are his ailing wife and a mute son. Isolated and adrift, the family faces a poignant existential crisis. As the English language begins to eclipse their own dialect and the villagers drift away from traditional rituals, Angba experiences deep psychological turmoil. The narrative captures the myriad challenges rural life faces amidst inevitable change, serving also as a deeply moving story about the bond between a father and son. Originally released as a short film made in 2021—which won an award at France's Clermont-Ferrand International Short Film Festival— Angh has now been expanded to a 103-minute feature length. Shot on 16mm film, it stars Anglong Konyak as the village chief, alongside Amah Konyak, Sobino Rengma, and Jenpai Konyak. Scottish actor Douglas Henshall portrays the American pastor. Henshall is globally acclaimed for his role as Detective Jimmy Perez in the British crime drama series Shetland (2013–2025). The screenplay was co-written by Theja and James Davis. Polish cinematographer Adam Pietkiewicz handled the film’s visuals, with editing by Tania Chhabria and music composed by Sagar Desai. Sound design was led by Susmit Nath and Anuroop Kukreja.
