items.title: Hyderabad: Meat waste thrown near Ganesh pandal triggers protest, 3 held
items.summary: Tension prevailed in Hyderabad’s Madannapet area on Sunday, September 20, over allegations that meat waste was thrown near a spot in a housing society where free food distribution was organised during the Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations. An FIR has been registered under sections related to promoting enmity and malicious acts following a complaint by a resident identified as Pilli Prasad. The incident flared up with the BJP leaders claiming that beef was thrown to provoke the Hindu religious sentiments. The BJP members and Hindu organisations staged protests at the Chanchalguda cross roads, seeking action against those responsible. Three persons including two women have since been arrested, according to reports. According to FIR, Pilli Prasad, a resident of the 2BHK Dignity Society in Madannapet, a free food distribution programme was organised near the Ganesh pandal as part of the Ganesh festivities in the society. At around 3 pm, while the devotees were having lunch, a resident identified as Mohammed Imran Qureshi, who was living on the 7th floor, allegedly threw meat waste near the food distribution point. Pilli Prasad claimed that the said act was “committed deliberately and with an intention to disturb the religious harmony and create tension and conflict” among the residents. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under sections 196 (2) (promoting enmity) and 299 (deliberate and malicious acts) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The police have sent the meat waste to the forensics department to establish if the discarded meat was beef, reports said.

items.title: Actor Radha accuses sister Ambika, brother of cheque fraud worth Rs 46 crore
items.summary: Actor Radha on Monday, September 21, filed a complaint with the Greater Chennai Police Commissioner against her elder sister, actor Ambika, and their brother, Mallikarjuna Kunjan Nair, alleging that signed blank cheques belonging to her were taken from her residence and misused in an attempt to claim around Rs 46 crore. Radha has alleged that the issue is linked to a wider family dispute over property and financial transactions. She said that she had kept a few signed blank cheques in her room for routine business expenses, such as salaries, utility bills, taxes, and garden maintenance, particularly when she was travelling. Radha said she maintained a current account with IDBI Bank for her business, which initially operated under the name ARS Garden Studio. After the business was renamed RR Gardens in January 2025, she received a new cheque book and stopped using the old one. She said she subsequently forgot about the unused cheques that remained at her residence. Radha said the bank informed her on September 17 that five of the old cheques had been presented for encashment in Ambika’s name, involving a total of around Rs 46 crore. She said she immediately instructed the bank to stop payment on the cheques. She alleged that she had never handed over the cheques to Ambika and had not entered into any financial transaction with her that would warrant such payments. Radha further alleged that the cheques had been filled out by her brother, Mallikarjuna, and claimed that Ambika and Mallikarjuna had acted together in attempting to use them for unlawful financial gain. She also alleged that the cheques were accessed from her room while she was away from Chennai. The complaint also refers to a dispute over family property. Radha has alleged that she has been prevented from entering the property for around one-and-a-half years, and that valuables, jewellery, property documents, and other records are kept there. Radha has sought a police investigation into the allegations and criminal action if the charges are established. The allegations in the complaint have not been adjudicated. Radha and Ambika were prominent actresses in Tamil cinema during the 1980s and have acted alongside leading stars, including Rajinikanth and Kamal Haasan. items.title: When criticism of a dead journalist turns into abuse, where is the line?
items.summary: Death is meant to be an exit, a full stop to the world’s qualms with a person. But on the internet, everything is up for scrutiny, whether or not the person can defend themselves anymore. After the untimely demise of noted Malayala Manorama journalist Jijo John Puthezhathu on September 9 in Kochi, the state has been witnessing an ethical paradox unfold– can the dead be mourned and still be condemned? In Jijo’s case, though, what is happening is more than condemnation. An onslaught of cruel cyber abuse targeting him and the integrity of his journalistic work has triggered police action at the request of his grieving family. The police have reportedly traced over 3000 abusive social media posts targeting him and humiliating his family on his behalf. The primary reason for the cyber lynching is that several people had quarrels with Jijo’s reporting, which is accused of being biased against the Left in Kerala. Some also allege his investigations for Malayalam Manorama to be targeted attacks on CPI(M)-leaning individuals and institutions, without enough evidence. Though most of his work, which is now being contested, was commissioned and published by his employer Manorama, a prominent legacy media giant in Kerala, the ire is directed towards Jijo and his family, rather than the establishment. The social media backlash, allegedly unleashed mostly by pro-Left handles, is personal and extremely brutal, prompting several journalists, even those who criticised his work, to call for empathy. The larger question that emerges now is about the fairness of the posthumous attack on a journalist for his work. At what point does criticism become relentless personal abuse, especially when directed at someone who is no longer alive? What other journalists say In 2020, Jijo had reported on the alleged benami holdings of M Sivasankar, former Principal Secretary to ex-Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan, in a Nagercoil wind farm project. Attributing the findings to the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Jijo reported that, with this, the ED’s probe into Sivasankar’s alleged involvement in the gold smuggling case would be further extended to Nagercoil. The report drew major criticism from several netizens and journalists for not verifying the claims. Sivasankar also filed a defamation case against Jijo, the verdict on which is yet to be pronounced.
